reversal_steps: Remove the WAF rule or rate limit rule blocking the endpoint
Or re-enable the route in the API Gateway
reversal_basis: API endpoint blocking is typically done via WAF rules, API Gateway route disabling, or reverse proxy configuration. All are software-configurable and reversible.
source_reference: OWASP API Security Top 10 — https://owasp.org/www-project-api-security/ | AWS API Gateway: Disabling endpoints
risk_if_not_reversed: API consumers receive 403/404 for the blocked endpoint

reversal_steps: Remove the WAF rule or server configuration blocking the HTTP method
reversal_basis: HTTP method restriction (PUT, DELETE, PATCH) is typically a WAF rule or web server configuration. These are configuration changes that are fully reversible.
source_reference: OWASP: HTTP Method restriction — https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/REST_Security_Cheat_Sheet.html
risk_if_not_reversed: API calls using the blocked HTTP method fail with 405 Method Not Allowed

reversal_steps: Remove the WAF rule or nginx/apache config blocking the User-Agent pattern
reversal_basis: User-Agent blocking is a WAF or web server configuration rule. It can be added/removed at any time.
source_reference: OWASP: Bot management — https://owasp.org/www-community/Bot_protection
risk_if_not_reversed: Legitimate requests from blocked User-Agent string are rejected

reversal_steps: Disable or remove the WAF rule from the rule group
AWS WAF: aws wafv2 update-rule-group
reversal_basis: WAF rules are software configurations. Individual signatures can be enabled/disabled. AWS WAF, Cloudflare, and ModSecurity all support per-rule management.
source_reference: AWS WAF: Rule groups — https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/waf-rule-groups.html
risk_if_not_reversed: Legitimate traffic matching the WAF pattern is blocked

reversal_steps: Disable bot rules in WAF or Cloudflare bot management settings
reversal_basis: Bot protection rules are WAF/CDN features that can be enabled/disabled via configuration. Disabling removes protection against automated attacks. Security team approval required.
source_reference: Cloudflare Bot Management — https://www.cloudflare.com/products/bot-management/ | OWASP Bot protection
risk_if_not_reversed: N/A — enabling bot protection is a hardening measure

reversal_steps: Remove or raise the rate limit rule in the API Gateway, WAF, or reverse proxy
reversal_basis: Rate limiting is a configurable policy in API Gateways (Kong, AWS API GW, NGINX), WAFs, and reverse proxies. Limits can be adjusted or removed at any time.
source_reference: OWASP: API Security — API4:2023 Unrestricted Resource Consumption — https://owasp.org/API-Security/editions/2023/en/0xa4-unrestricted-resource-consumption/
risk_if_not_reversed: Legitimate high-volume API consumers are throttled

reversal_steps: Remove firewall rule blocking the protocol
Or re-enable the protocol in the network device configuration
reversal_basis: Network protocol blocking is enforced via firewall rules (iptables, AWS Security Groups, Azure NSG). Rules are deletable configuration entries.
source_reference: NIST 800-53 SC-7 Boundary Protection | CIS Controls v8 12.2
risk_if_not_reversed: All traffic using the blocked protocol is dropped

reversal_steps: Disable API key requirement in API Gateway settings
Note: Requires security review — removing API authentication is a compliance violation
reversal_basis: API authentication requirements are API Gateway configuration settings. Toggling is possible but disabling violates OWASP API Security API2:2023 (Authentication) and compliance requirements.
source_reference: OWASP API Security API2:2023 — https://owasp.org/API-Security/ | NIST 800-53 IA-3
risk_if_not_reversed: N/A — enabling API authentication is a security hardening measure

reversal_steps: Remove CAPTCHA challenge rule from WAF or application layer
reversal_basis: CAPTCHA challenges are WAF or application-level rules that can be toggled. They add a verification step for suspected bot traffic.
source_reference: OWASP: Bot Management — https://owasp.org/www-community/Bot_protection
risk_if_not_reversed: Legitimate users face CAPTCHA friction on the affected endpoint

reversal_steps: Trigger CI/CD rollback pipeline
Or: git revert <commit-hash> && deploy
Or: kubectl rollout undo deployment/<name>
reversal_basis: Code deployment rollback re-deploys a prior version. Git revert creates a new commit that undoes the change. Kubernetes rollouts maintain revision history (--revision flag) allowing rollback to any prior version.
source_reference: K8s: Deployment rollback — https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/workloads/controllers/deployment/#rolling-back-a-deployment | Git: git revert — https://git-scm.com/docs/git-revert
risk_if_not_reversed: Potentially vulnerable code version remains deployed

reversal_steps: Application restart is self-completing — no reversal needed
reversal_basis: Application restart clears in-memory state and reloads configuration. It is a standard operational procedure with no lasting data change. Sessions may be lost if not using persistent session store.
source_reference: NIST SP 800-61r2 §3.3 Incident Containment — https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/SpecialPublications/NIST.SP.800-61r2.pdf
risk_if_not_reversed: N/A — restart is self-completing

reversal_steps: Disable session recording in PAM tool (CyberArk, BeyondTrust) or monitoring platform
reversal_basis: Session recording is a PAM/monitoring configuration setting. Enabling records privileged sessions. Disabling stops new recordings. Existing recordings are preserved.
source_reference: CIS Controls v8 8.5 | NIST 800-53 AU-12 Audit Record Generation
risk_if_not_reversed: N/A — session recording is a hardening/audit measure

reversal_steps: Toggle maintenance mode flag off via application admin panel or platform configuration
reversal_basis: Maintenance mode is a feature flag that redirects user traffic to a static maintenance page. Disabling it immediately restores normal application routing.
source_reference: SOC 2 A1.1 Availability — https://www.aicpa.org/resources/article/trust-services-criteria
risk_if_not_reversed: Application is unavailable to all users — SLA/availability impact

reversal_steps: Re-enable the feature flag in the feature flag management system (LaunchDarkly, Flagsmith, AWS AppConfig)
reversal_basis: Feature flags are runtime configuration toggles. Disabling makes a feature unavailable. Re-enabling restores it. Changes take effect in seconds without deployment.
source_reference: Martin Fowler: Feature toggles — https://martinfowler.com/articles/feature-toggles.html
risk_if_not_reversed: Feature is unavailable to users

reversal_steps: Remove the firewall or proxy rule blocking the package registry
Or re-enable the package in the artifact repository allowlist
reversal_basis: Package registry blocking is implemented via network firewall rules or artifact repository policies. These are software configurations reversible by removing the block rule.
source_reference: NIST 800-53 CM-7 Least Functionality | CISA Supply Chain Security — https://www.cisa.gov/publication/defending-against-software-supply-chain-attacks
risk_if_not_reversed: Build pipelines cannot download dependencies — CI/CD failures

reversal_steps: Re-enable the webhook in the application settings or API platform
Verify webhook endpoint is secure before re-enabling after an incident
reversal_basis: Webhooks are configurable integrations that can be enabled/disabled via platform settings. Re-enabling restores event-driven integrations.
source_reference: OWASP: Webhook security — https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Input_Validation_Cheat_Sheet.html
risk_if_not_reversed: Event notifications to the webhook consumer stop

reversal_steps: Re-enable the integration in the platform admin settings
Verify integration security before re-enabling after a supply chain incident
reversal_basis: Third-party integrations can be disabled/re-enabled via platform admin settings. Re-enabling after a supply chain incident requires security review of the third-party.
source_reference: NIST 800-53 SA-9 External System Services | ISO 27001 A.5.19
risk_if_not_reversed: Third-party functionality is unavailable to users

reversal_steps: If package was mis-identified, remove it from quarantine in the artifact repository (Artifactory, Nexus, ECR)
reversal_basis: Package quarantine moves a package to an isolated repository space. Restoration requires security team review to confirm the package is safe before restoring to the active feed.
source_reference: CISA: Software Supply Chain Security — https://www.cisa.gov/publication/defending-against-software-supply-chain-attacks | JFrog Xray quarantine
risk_if_not_reversed: Builds requiring the quarantined package will fail

reversal_steps: Disable PAM enforcement via the PAM tool administration console
Note: Requires CISO approval — disabling PAM removes a critical security control
reversal_basis: PAM enforcement is a platform-level configuration. Disabling allows privileged access without PAM controls. This is a critical compliance-relevant action requiring CISO-level approval.
source_reference: CIS Controls v8 5.3 / 6.8 | NIST 800-53 AC-6 Least Privilege
risk_if_not_reversed: N/A — enabling PAM is a hardening measure

reversal_steps: Remove the registry modification block via GPO, EDR policy, or host-based firewall rule
reversal_basis: Registry modification blocking is enforced via GPO (Windows Registry policies), AppLocker, or EDR behavioral rules. These are policy configurations that can be reverted.
source_reference: CIS Benchmarks: Windows Registry hardening | NIST 800-53 CM-7 Least Functionality
risk_if_not_reversed: Legitimate application installers and system tools that require registry writes will fail

reversal_steps: Disable auditd (Linux: systemctl stop auditd) or kernel logging configuration
reversal_basis: Kernel logging (Linux auditd, Windows kernel audit events) is a configuration that can be enabled/disabled. Disabling after an incident removes forensic visibility. Security team approval required.
source_reference: Linux auditd: https://linux-audit.com/linux-audit-framework-basics/ | NIST 800-53 AU-12
risk_if_not_reversed: N/A — enabling kernel logging is a forensic/audit hardening measure
